problems.title: Factor before substituting
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt{(x^4y^2-x^2y^4)/(x^2-y^2)}$ at $x=3,y=6$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Since $x^2\ne y^2$, cancel the common factor. The radical is $\sqrt{x^2y^2}=|xy|$.
At the given values this is 18.

problems.title: A tangent and a secant
problems.question: A tangent has length 20 cm and the external part of a secant is 16 cm. Find its internal part.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: $400=16(16+i)$, so the whole secant length is 25 and the internal part is $25-16=9$.

problems.title: A nested radical
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt{11-6\sqrt2}$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The square root is $|3-\sqrt2|$. Since $3>\sqrt2$, this is $3-\sqrt2$.

problems.title: A median perpendicular to an angle bisector
problems.question: In triangle $ABC$, median $BE$ is perpendicular to bisector $AD$. Find $AB$ if $AC=14$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: An angle-bisector direction makes equal angles with $AB,AC$; perpendicular vectors have equal projections along that direction when their connecting line is perpendicular to it.
steps: Let $AB=u,AC=v$, and half-angle at $A$ be $\theta$. Projection of $B$ along $AD$ is $u\cos\theta$. Since $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$, its projection is $(v/2)\cos\theta$.
$BE\perp AD$ makes these projections equal. As $\cos\theta>0$, $u=v/2=7$.

problems.title: Extract a fourth power correctly
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt[4]{a^6b^7c^5}$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The general factored expression is $|abc|\sqrt[4]{a^2b^3c}$.
If $a\ne0$, the original real domain requires $bc\ge0$, so $|abc|=|a|bc$. If $a=0$, both expressions are zero, including when $bc<0$.
problems.answer: $|a|bc\sqrt[4]{a^2b^3c}$, on the original real domain (choice გ).

problems.title: One worker’s daily rate
problems.question: $m$ equally productive workers build a wall in $k$ days. What fraction does one worker build in one day?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: Total worker-days $=mk$; one whole job divided by worker-days gives individual daily rate.
steps: The wall requires $mk$ worker-days. One worker-day completes $1/(mk)$ of it.

problems.title: A radical numerator that doubles the denominator
problems.question: Evaluate $(\sqrt{13}+\sqrt7)^2/(10+\sqrt{91})$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The numerator is $20+2\sqrt{91}=2(10+\sqrt{91})$. The denominator is positive, so cancellation gives 2.

problems.title: Midpoints of trapezoid diagonals
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 9 and 17. Find the distance between its diagonal midpoints.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The segment joining diagonal midpoints is parallel to the bases and has length half their difference.
steps: For verification, use $A=0,D=d,B=u,C=u+c$. The two diagonal midpoints are $(u+c)/2$ and $(u+d)/2$, whose difference is $(d-c)/2$.
The distance is $(17-9)/2=4$.

problems.title: Highest power of seven in a factorial
problems.question: Find the largest $n$ for which $7^n$ divides $50!$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The exponent is $\lfloor50/7\rfloor+\lfloor50/49\rfloor=7+1=8$.

problems.title: A weighted concentration
problems.question: Mix 6 litres of 20% alcohol with 2 litres of 40% alcohol. Find the resulting percentage.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Pure alcohol totals $6(0.2)+2(0.4)=2$ litres. The mixture totals 8 litres.
The concentration is $2/8=25\%$.

problems.title: A bisector halves a trapezoid leg
problems.question: Right trapezoid $ABCD$ has $A=90^\circ$, $AB=AD+BC$. The bisector of $ABC$ meets $CD$ at $K$. Find $CK:KD$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The right-angle bisector at $B$ is $y=h-x$. On $CD$, write $K=(c+t(d-c),h(1-t))$.
Substitute into the bisector equation: $ht=c+t(d-c)$, so $t(h-d+c)=c$. Since $h=c+d$, $t=1/2$.

problems.title: A natural-number divisibility condition
problems.question: $p,q$ are natural numbers and $p/6+q/10$ is a natural number. Which listed $p$ can work?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Divisibility by 3 requires $2p\equiv0\pmod3$, hence $p$ is a multiple of 3.
Only 3 is listed. It works with $q=5$, giving $3/6+5/10=1$.

problems.title: An angle equal to an angle between bisectors
problems.question: Angle $A$ equals one of the angles formed by the bisectors from $B,C$. Find $A$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: At the incenter, the two angle sizes are $90^\circ+A/2$ and $90^\circ-A/2$.
steps: $A=90^\circ+A/2$ gives $A=180^\circ$, impossible for a triangle.
$A=90^\circ-A/2$ gives $3A/2=90^\circ$, so $A=60^\circ$.

problems.title: A factorial sum modulo sixty
problems.question: Find the remainder of $1!+2!+\cdots+525!$ modulo 60.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: $5!=120$ is divisible by 60, and so is every later factorial.
steps: Only the first four terms matter: $1+2+6+24=33$.

problems.title: A long base-angle bisector in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: $AB=AC$ and the bisector $BL$ has twice the length of altitude $AD$. Find the angles.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Let the equal sides be $s$ and base angle $B=\beta$. Then $BC=2s\cos\beta$, so $BL=4s\cos\beta\cos(\beta/2)/(1+2\cos\beta)$.
Set this equal to $2s\sin\beta$ and put $u=\sin(\beta/2)$. Cancelling positive factors gives $4u^3-2u^2-3u+1=(u-1)(4u^2+2u-1)=0$.
Because $0<\beta<90^\circ$, the valid root is $u=(\sqrt5-1)/4=\sin18^\circ$. Thus $\beta=36^\circ$ and the apex angle is $108^\circ$.

problems.title: Principal complex square roots
problems.question: Find $y-1$ if $y=\sqrt{-3}\sqrt{-7}/\sqrt{(-3)(-7)}$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The numerator is $-\sqrt{21}$ and denominator is $\sqrt{21}$, so $y=-1$. Thus $y-1=-2$.
problems.note: The real-number product rule for square roots cannot be applied indiscriminately to negative complex inputs.

problems.title: Increase a radical expression by a percentage
problems.question: By what percentage must $\sqrt{3a^2}/\sqrt7$ increase to become $\sqrt{300a^2}/\sqrt{28}$, $a\ne0$?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The new value is five times the old one. The increase is four times the old value, or 400%.

problems.title: Bisected segments force an equilateral triangle
problems.question: $AM$ is a median, $BH$ an altitude, $CN$ an angle bisector. Segments $CN,MH$ bisect each other. Find the triangle angles.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is a parallelogram; midpoint theorem; angle-bisector theorem.
steps: The quadrilateral $CMNH$ has diagonals $CN,MH$, hence is a parallelogram. Thus $MN\parallel CH\parallel AC$. Since $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $N$ is the midpoint of $BA$.
Also $NH\parallel CM\parallel BC$, so $H$ is the midpoint of $AC$. Altitude $BH$ is therefore a median, giving $BA=BC$.
Bisector $CN$ is a median too, giving $CA=CB$. All three sides are equal.

problems.title: Equal ratios combine into a sum ratio
problems.question: $a/m=b/n=c/k=8/11$. Find $2(m+n+k)/(a+b+c)$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Substitute and cancel the common nonzero sum to get $2/(8/11)=11/4$.
problems.answer: $11/4$, provided the printed fraction is defined.
problems.note: If the common sum is zero, the requested quotient is undefined. The standard intended interpretation assumes a nonzero denominator.

problems.title: A product just below a square
problems.question: $x=2017\cdot2019\cdot2021\cdot2023+16$. Which natural number squared equals $x$?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The positive square root is $2020^2-5$.

problems.title: Count integer outputs, not inputs
problems.question: How many different integer values can $x^3/x$ take for $x\in(-3,4]$?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The original expression excludes $x=0$ and otherwise equals $x^2$.
steps: On the given domain the output range is $(0,16]$. Every value occurs, for example through positive $x\le4$.
The integer outputs are 1 through 16.

problems.title: A second tangent meets a diameter-end tangent
problems.question: $AC$ is a circle diameter; $BC$ is tangent at $C$. Segment $AB$ meets the circle again at $D$, and the tangent at $D$ meets $BC$ at $K$. Find $BK:KC$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The second intersection of line $AB$ is $D=(8r^3/(4r^2+t^2),4r^2t/(4r^2+t^2))$.
The tangent at $D$ has equation $(D_x-r)(x-r)+D_y y=r^2$. At $x=2r$, substitution simplifies to $y=t/2$.
Thus $K=(2r,t/2)$ is the midpoint of $BC$.

problems.title: Integer values of a rational expression
problems.question: For how many integers $n$ is $3n/(n+2)$ an integer?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The nonzero integer $n+2$ must divide 6. Its choices are $\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,\pm6$.
Each gives one distinct $n$, for eight total.

problems.title: A set of primes
problems.question: A finite set contains only prime numbers, and 2% of its elements are divisible by 17. Find its size.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The only prime divisible by 17 is 17 itself.
steps: A set cannot repeat elements, so exactly one element is divisible by 17. If the size is $N$, then $0.02N=1$.
Thus $N=50$.

problems.title: Savings over an integer number of days
problems.question: Daily earnings $a\in(17,19)$ and spending $b\in(9,10)$ produce total savings 33. How many days were worked?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: If the number of days is $d$, then $7d<33<10d$, so $3.3<d<33/7$.
The only integer is 4. It is achievable with daily savings $33/4=8.25$ in the allowed range.

problems.title: A divisor common to all even inputs
problems.question: Find the greatest natural number dividing $4m^2+6n^2$ for every even $m,n$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Every value is divisible by 8. To rule out a larger common divisor, take positive even pairs $(m,n)=(2,2)$ and $(2,4)$. They give 40 and 112, whose GCD is 8.
Thus no integer larger than 8 can divide every value.

problems.title: An inverse percentage change
problems.question: $a,b>0$, $ab=199$. If $a$ increases by 60% while the product stays fixed, how does $b$ change?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.

problems.title: Right angles in a convex octagon
problems.question: What is the maximum number of right interior angles in a convex octagon?
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The exterior angles of a strictly convex polygon are positive and sum to $360^\circ$.
steps: Each right interior angle contributes an exterior turn of $90^\circ$. Four would use all $360^\circ$, leaving no positive turns for the other four vertices, so at most three are possible.

Three can occur: begin with a rectangle and replace one corner by a convex chain of five small turns totalling $90^\circ$. The other three corners remain right angles and the result has eight vertices.

problems.title: Oddness and periodicity
problems.question: $f$ is odd and has period 5. Given $f(1)=2$, find $f(9)$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.

problems.title: Which graphs can be drawn in one stroke?
problems.question: Choose the ordered triple: an Euler circuit startable anywhere, an open Euler trail with a prescribed start, and a graph with no one-stroke drawing.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: A connected graph has an Euler circuit iff all degrees are even; it has an open Euler trail iff exactly two degrees are odd.
steps: Graph IV consists of overlapping rectangle outlines. Every corner has degree 2 and every crossing degree 4, so all degrees are even.
Graph II has exactly two odd vertices: the central meeting point on the horizontal top and the central bottom point. Start at either and finish at the other.
Graph V has four odd vertices (the two outer roof-base corners, central roof-base junction and central bottom junction), so no Euler trail exists.
problems.note: Crossings in the drawing are treated as graph vertices; each edge is traversed once.

problems.title: Perimeter of a tangential right trapezoid
problems.question: $A=B=90^\circ$, incircle radius $\sqrt3$, centre-to-$C$ distance 2, and $ADC=60^\circ$. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: $h=2r$; sloping leg $l=h/\sin60^\circ$; in a tangential quadrilateral, base sum equals leg sum.
steps: The perpendicular leg is $h=2\sqrt3$, and the sloping leg is $2\sqrt3/(\sqrt3/2)=4$.
The perimeter is twice their sum: $P=4\sqrt3+8$.
The given $OC=2$ is consistent: angle $C=120^\circ$, so $OC=r/\sin60^\circ=2$.

problems.title: Intercepts of a composed function
problems.question: $f(x)=3x^2$, $g(x)=2x-1$. Find the axis intercepts of $f(g(x))$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: For an $x$-axis intercept set the output to zero: $2x-1=0$, so the point is $(1/2,0)$.
For the $y$-axis intercept set $x=0$, giving $(0,3)$.

problems.title: Equal sides reveal a fixed angle
problems.question: $D$ lies on $AC$ with $AD=AB$, and $CBA-ACB=30^\circ$. Find $CBD$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Let $C=\gamma$, so $B=\gamma+30^\circ$ and $A=150^\circ-2\gamma$.
Then $ABD=(180^\circ-A)/2=15^\circ+\gamma$. Subtract from $ABC$: $CBD=(\gamma+30^\circ)-(\gamma+15^\circ)=15^\circ$.

problems.title: Maximize a ratio with bounded variables
problems.question: Find the maximum of $(a+b)/(a-b)$ for $5\le a\le8$, $2\le b\le4$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: For fixed $b$, increasing $a$ enlarges the denominator and decreases the ratio. For fixed $a$, increasing $b$ increases the numerator and decreases the positive denominator.
Thus the maximum is at $a=5,b=4$, giving $9/1=9$.

problems.title: Return a fraction to the same value
problems.question: Start at $5/6$. Each operation adds 4 to the numerator or 7 to the denominator. Find the fewest positive number of operations that returns an equal fraction.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Cross-multiplication gives $24u=35v$. Since 24 and 35 are coprime, $u=35k,v=24k$ for a nonnegative integer $k$.
The smallest nonzero choice is $k=1$, giving $35+24=59$ operations.

problems.title: A parallel line outside a trapezoid
problems.question: $AB=BC$, $AC=AD$ in trapezoid $ABCD$ with $BC$ the shorter base. Through $B$, draw $BM\parallel AC$ meeting line $DC$ at $M$. Given $BCA=40^\circ$, find $BMA$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: Equal sides imply equal opposite angles; parallel-line angle relations.
steps: Triangle $ABC$ has angles $A=C=40^\circ$, so $ABC=100^\circ$. Also $CAD=40^\circ$, and $AC=AD$ makes $ACD=ADC=70^\circ$.
The intersection $M$ lies beyond $C$ on ray $DC$. In triangle $BCM$, $CBM=40^\circ$ and $BCM=70^\circ$, so $BMC=70^\circ$. Therefore $BM=BC=AB$.
At $B$, $ABM=100^\circ+40^\circ=140^\circ$. Isosceles $ABM$ has base angles $(180^\circ-140^\circ)/2=20^\circ$.

problems.title: A parallel segment through an altitude point
problems.question: $AB=BC=4,AC=3$. On altitude $BM$, $BK:KM=3:7$. A line through $K$ parallel to $AB$ meets $AC,BC$ at $D,E$. Find $DE$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Choose $A=(-1.5,0),C=(1.5,0),B=(0,H)$. Then $K=(0,0.7H)$. A line parallel to $AB$ has equation $y=0.7H+(H/1.5)x$.

problems.title: An altitude foot, an incenter and a tangency point
problems.question: $CD$ bisects angle $C$, $BM\perp CD$, $M\in CD$. The incircle touches $BC$ at $K$. If $BAC=\alpha$, find $MKB$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: If $I$ is the incenter, $BIC=90^\circ+\alpha/2$; opposite right angles imply concyclicity.
steps: $I$ lies on $CD$. Both $BM\perp IM$ and $BK\perp IK$ are right angles, so $B,M,I,K$ lie on the circle with diameter $BI$.
Since $BIC$ is obtuse, the foot $M$ is on the opposite side of $I$ from $C$. Thus $MIB=180^\circ-BIC=90^\circ-\alpha/2$.
Angles $MKB$ and $MIB$ subtend the same chord $MB$ on this circle, giving the requested angle.

problems.title: Last two digits of a power sum
problems.question: Find the last two digits of $2009^{2018}+2009^{2019}$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: Factor the common power; compute modulo 100.
steps: The sum is $2010\cdot2009^{2018}$. Modulo 100 this is $10\cdot9^{2018}$.
Only the last digit of $9^{2018}$ matters after multiplication by 10. It is 1 because the exponent is even. Thus the remainder modulo 100 is 10.

problems.title: Solve an equation with an even periodic function
problems.question: $f$ is even with period 6 and $f(t)=t^2-4t+3$ on $[0,3]$. Solve $f(x+2)f(x+8)-f(x+14)-2=0$.
problems.idea: Set up the relation first, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: Periodicity makes all three function values equal; on $[0,3]$, $f(t)=(t-2)^2-1$.
steps: In $[0,3]$, $f(t)=2$ gives $t=2-\sqrt3$ (the other quadratic root exceeds 3), and $f(t)=-1$ gives $t=2$.
Evenness and period 6 give $x+2=6k\pm(2-\sqrt3)$ or $x+2=6k\pm2$, for any integer $k$.
